# HE-C1 — Theories and principles of assessment in HE

Annex F gives this line **13 items** (Remember 1, Understand 2, Apply 7, Analyze 2, Evaluate 1). Outcomes: **competency-based assessment tools**; **authentic assessment in TLE**; **using assessment data to improve instruction**. [SRC-0002, Annex F, C.1] ProfEd D (assessment of learning) covers test construction and statistics; this lesson covers the TVET and performance side.

## 1. Plain explanation

**Competency-based assessment (CBA)** asks one question: can the learner perform the task to the industry standard? The answer is **competent** or **not yet competent**, judged from evidence against a unit of competency. TESDA's assessor follows six steps: organize, prepare the candidate, gather evidence, decide, record, give feedback.

**Assessment for learning vs of learning.** Formative assessment happens during instruction to adjust teaching; summative happens after, to certify and grade.

**Performance assessment** has learners do a complex task (cook a dish, sew a garment, repair a machine) while the teacher judges both the **process** and the **product**. **Authentic** assessment is a task close to real-world work. **Alternative** assessment simply means not pencil-and-paper.

**Rubrics** make judgments consistent: **holistic** (one overall score) or **analytic** (separate scores per criterion).

**Portfolios** are purposeful collections that tell the story of achievement or growth.

**Data use.** Results show which competencies are weak, so the teacher re-teaches, gives more practice, and offers reassessment.

## 2. Testable facts

**Conducting competency assessment (TESDA Trainers Methodology Level I, "Conduct competency assessment")**
- Elements: (1) **organize** assessment activities; (2) **prepare the candidate**; (3) **gather evidence**; (4) **make the assessment decision**; (5) **record** results; (6) **provide feedback**. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit]
- Preparing the candidate: explain the **context and purpose**, determine needs for **allowable adjustments**, explain legal and ethical responsibilities, the **competency standards** and evidence to be collected, and the procedure. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, element 2]
- Evidence is gathered using the methods in the **Evidence Guide**, with **reasonable adjustments** where appropriate, and documented with the relevant tools. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, element 3]
- The decision evaluates evidence against the **rules of evidence** and the **dimensions of competency**, and the requirements of the unit(s) of competency. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, element 4]
- Records and **confidentiality** of outcomes are kept per policy; issuing of certificates is organized. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, element 5]
- Feedback is clear and constructive; **gaps are explored** with the candidate; the candidate is advised of **reassessment**; disputed decisions are recorded and reported. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, element 6]
- Purposes of assessment listed: **certify competency**, recruit and select, monitor performance, determine **training needs**, skills audit, **recognize prior learning (RPL)**, classify against industry standards, and **give feedback on progress** during training. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, range of variables 1]
- Evidence may be **direct** or **indirect**. [SRC-0081, conduct competency assessment unit, range of variables 2]
- When planning a session, trainers select assessment methods that fit the module's learning outcome and check instruments for **validity, fairness, safety and cost-effectiveness**. [SRC-0081, plan training session unit, elements 4.3–4.5]
- Methods of assessment used across TM units include **demonstration/observation with oral questioning**, written tests, interviews, **third-party reports** and **portfolios**. [SRC-0081, evidence guides, "methods of assessment"]

**Basic concepts (Seifert & Sutton Ch. 11)**
- **Assessment** gathers information about learning and makes value judgments; **measurement** answers "how much?" (assigning numbers); **evaluation** makes judgments about the information. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Basic concepts"]
- **Assessment for learning** is usually **formative** (during instruction, to revise teaching and improve learning); **assessment of learning** is usually **summative** (after instruction, to certify and grade). [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Basic concepts"]
- Formative assessment can be **informal** (spontaneous observation during Q&A or seatwork) or **formal** (planned, systematic data gathering). [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Basic concepts"]

**Performance and authentic assessment**
- In **performance assessment**, students complete a complex task while the teacher observes the **process or procedure** as well as the **product**; examples include repairing a machine, conducting an experiment, artistic creation. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Performance assessments"]
- **Alternative assessment** = tasks that are not pencil-and-paper. **Authentic assessment** = tasks similar to those in the **real world**; authenticity is a matter of degree. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Performance assessments"]
- Advantages: assess **complex outcomes**, assess **process and product**, communicate goals clearly, and usually have **good content validity**. Disadvantages: **time-consuming** (so fewer tasks) and **hard to score reliably**. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Advantages and disadvantages"]

**Rubrics**
- **Holistic rubric:** general descriptions and **one overall score**; quicker to develop. **Analytic rubric:** levels described for **each characteristic** separately (e.g. six writing traits), giving more specific feedback. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Scoring rubrics"]

**Portfolios**
- A portfolio is "a meaningful collection of student work that tells the story of student achievement or growth" — **purposeful**, not a folder of everything. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Portfolios"]
- Four dimensions of purpose: assessment **for** vs **of** learning; **current accomplishments** vs **progress**; **best-work showcase** vs **documentation**; **finished** vs **working**. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Portfolios"]
- Showcase portfolios hold **best work**, usually chosen by the student; documentation portfolios include **all** work samples; working portfolios hold day-to-day work and are **not** meant for assessment of learning. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Portfolios"]

**Qualifications and certification**
- The **Philippine Qualifications Framework** (RA 10968) describes levels of qualifications and sets standards for outcomes; its level descriptors are defined by **knowledge, skills and values; application; degree of independence**. [SRC-0042, Secs. 4, 8]
- The PQF harmonizes qualification levels across **basic, technical-vocational and higher education** and supports **recognition of prior learning**. [SRC-0042, Secs. 5, 8]
- TESDA-accredited **industry committees** set national occupational skills standards, and accredited bodies conduct trade tests for certification. [SRC-0043, Sec. 22]

## 3. Common mistakes

- **Competency results are "competent / not yet competent"**, not ranked scores.
- **Authentic ≠ alternative.** An essay is alternative to MCQ in some sense but not necessarily authentic; cooking for real customers is highly authentic.
- **Performance assessment judges process too.** Watching the knife technique matters, not only tasting the dish.
- **Holistic = one score; analytic = several.** Use analytic when you need diagnostic feedback.
- **Working portfolio is not for grading.**
- **RPL** is a purpose of assessment: certifying skills already gained outside formal training.
- **Formative is not "ungraded quiz" only;** its defining feature is that results are used to adjust teaching during instruction.

## 4. Memory aid

**TESDA assessor "O-P-G-D-R-F"**: Organize, Prepare, Gather, Decide, Record, Feedback — "Only Prepared Grads Do Real Fieldwork."
**Portfolio pairs "For/Of, Now/Growth, Best/All, Done/Working."**

## 5. Sources

- SRC-0081 TESDA Trainers Methodology Level I (conduct competency assessment; plan training session)
- SRC-0109 Seifert & Sutton, *Educational Psychology* 2e (CC BY 3.0), Ch. 11
- SRC-0042 RA 10968 (PQF); SRC-0043 RA 7796
- SRC-0002 Res. 20 s. 2025 Annex F

title: Basic research in Home Economics — parts of a research paper, variables and sampling, action research, using findings
md:
# HE-D1 — Basic research in Home Economics

Annex F gives this line **8 items** (Remember 1, Understand 1, Apply 4, Analyze 1, Evaluate 1). Outcomes: **parts of a research paper**; **action research methods** in HE; **using research findings** to improve HE teaching. [SRC-0002, Annex F, D.1] ProfEd E2 (action research) overlaps.

## 1. Plain explanation

**A research article** usually follows **IMRaD**: Introduction (why, research question), Methods (who, when, where, how), Results (what was found), Discussion (what it means and what next).

**Research vocabulary.** The **population** is everyone you want to know about; the **sample** is the group you actually study. A **parameter** describes the population; a **statistic** describes the sample. Data are **qualitative** (categories, words) or **quantitative** (counts and measurements).

**Sampling.** Random methods are simple random, **stratified** (random within each subgroup), **cluster** (randomly pick whole groups), and **systematic** (every nth). **Convenience** sampling is non-random and can be biased.

**Experiments.** The **explanatory (independent)** variable is what you change; the **response (dependent)** variable is what you measure. A **control group** and **blinding** guard against bias; **lurking variables** can confuse results.

**Action research** is teacher research on one's own class: plan (identify the problem, review literature, plan data collection) → act (collect and analyze data) → develop an action plan → communicate and reflect, then repeat.

**Ethics.** Get **informed consent** when data will be shared outside the school; participation in research is voluntary; protect privacy.

## 2. Testable facts

**Parts of a research paper**
- **IMRaD = Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion**, the most common structure for original research articles. [SRC-0168, lead]
- Introduction: why the study was done, the research question or hypothesis. Methods: who, when, where and how, materials and participants. Results: what answer was found; was the hypothesis supported. Discussion: implications, fit with other research, future research. [SRC-0168, "Overview"]
- The IMRaD flow is often pictured as a **"wine glass" (hourglass) model**: from general (introduction) to specific (methods, results) and back to general (discussion). [SRC-0168, "Overview"]
- Other common elements outside the acronym include **disclosure statements** (funding, conflicts of interest) and **ethical compliance statements**. [SRC-0168, "Other elements"]

**Population, sample and data (OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e)**
- A **statistic** is a number describing a property of the **sample**; a **parameter** describes the **population**. [SRC-0091, 1.1]
- **Qualitative (categorical) data** come from categorizing or describing attributes, usually words or letters; **quantitative data** come from counting or measuring and are always numbers (discrete or continuous). Pie charts and bar graphs display qualitative data. [SRC-0091, 1.2]
- **Stratified sample:** divide the population into strata and take a proportionate random sample from **each** stratum. **Cluster sample:** divide into clusters and randomly select **some clusters**, taking all their members. **Systematic sample:** random start, then **every nth** item from a list. [SRC-0091, 1.2]
- **Convenience sampling** uses readily available results; it is **non-random** and may be highly biased. [SRC-0091, 1.2]

**Experimental design**
- The **explanatory variable** causes change in the **response variable**; **lurking variables** are other variables that can cloud the study, so the explanatory variable must be isolated. [SRC-0091, 1.4]
- A **control group** balances the effects of being in an experiment; **blinding** counters the power of suggestion; in a **double-blind** experiment both subjects and the researchers dealing with them are blinded. [SRC-0091, 1.4]
- Participants must give **informed consent**. [SRC-0091, 1.4 "Ethics"]

**Action research**
- **Kurt Lewin** coined "action research" in **1944**; he described "a spiral of steps, each of which is composed of a circle of **planning, action and fact-finding** about the result of the action". [SRC-0169, lead]
- **Action research (teacher research):** investigation by teachers of their own students or their own teaching, leading to **concrete decisions** that improve teaching and learning in a particular context. [SRC-0109, Ch. 1 "New trend #4: increased professionalism of teachers"]
- Compared with ordinary good teaching, action research is **planned more thoughtfully, recorded more systematically, and shared more openly** with colleagues. [SRC-0109, Ch. 1, after Table 1]
- Mertler's cycle: **Planning** (identify and define the problem; review related literature; develop a research plan of what data, how and when) → **Acting** (collect and analyze data; keep it manageable) → **Developing an action plan** (make and document changes) → **Communicating and reflecting** ("What did I learn? What should I do next?"), which starts a new cycle. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Cycles of planning, acting and reflecting"]
- Data in action research can include student work, observation, **videotaping one's own lessons**, a **journal diary**, and **interviews**. [SRC-0109, Ch. 1 Table 1]

**Ethics and privacy**
- If action-research data will be shared **outside the school community**, permission from **parents or guardians and students** is needed, usually via an **informed consent form** that describes the study and data, states participation is **voluntary**, and guarantees **confidentiality or anonymity**. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Ethical issues"]
- Students may **choose not to participate** in research, unlike ordinary class tasks. [SRC-0109, Ch. 11 "Ethical issues"]
- Learners' **education and health** information is sensitive personal information under RA 10173. [SRC-0045, Sec. 3(l)]

## 3. Common mistakes

- **Methods vs Results.** "We surveyed 40 Grade 8 learners using a 20-item checklist" is Methods; "68% preferred…" is Results; "This suggests that…" is Discussion.
- **Stratified vs cluster.** Stratified samples from *every* group; cluster takes *whole* groups chosen at random.
- **Convenience sampling is not random**, even if it is easy and large.
- **Statistic ↔ sample; parameter ↔ population.** (S–S, P–P.)
- **Independent = explanatory; dependent = response.**
- **Action research starts with a classroom problem**, not with a hypothesis from a textbook; it ends with action and reflection, not only a report.
- **Consent:** research participation is voluntary; class activities are not.

## 4. Memory aid

**"I Must Report Discoveries"** = Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion.
**Action research "Plan–Act–Change–Share/Reflect" (PACS).**
**Sampling "Strata = Some of every group; Cluster = Choose whole groups."**

## 5. Sources

- SRC-0168 IMRAD; SRC-0169 Action research — Wikipedia (tertiary)
- SRC-0091 OpenStax *Introductory Statistics 2e* 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
- SRC-0109 Seifert & Sutton, *Educational Psychology* 2e (CC BY 3.0), Ch. 1, Ch. 11
- SRC-0045 RA 10173 Sec. 3(l)
- SRC-0002 Res. 20 s. 2025 Annex F

title: Foundations of teaching and learning — social foundations and inclusive education
md:
# PE-A1 — Foundations: social foundations and inclusive education

The outline asks you to "apply philosophical and sociological principles in teaching-learning situations" and "apply foundation theories of special and inclusive education" [SRC-0001, ProfEd Section A, outcomes 1.1–1.2]. This lesson covers the **sociological** foundations, the **legal and historical** foundations, and **inclusive education** under Philippine law. *Philosophies of education* are pending (see the gaps note at the end).

## 1. Plain explanation

**Three sociological lenses** explain what schools do.
- **Functionalism** sees education as a key social institution with *manifest* functions (intended and visible, such as socialization and social control) and *latent* functions (hidden and unintended, such as friendships, networks and teamwork).
- **Conflict theory** sees schooling as widening inequality, through the *hidden curriculum* and *tracking*.
- **Symbolic interactionism** studies classroom interaction and labeling, which can create self-fulfilling prophecies. **Feminist theory** examines gender inequality in education.

**Inclusive education** is now law. RA 11650 (2022) requires every public and private early and basic education school to admit and serve learners with disabilities. It uses tools such as the **Child Find System**, the **Individualized Education Plan (IEP)** and **Inclusive Learning Resource Centers (ILRCs)**, which replace the old SPED Centers.

**The Constitution** guarantees the right to quality education. It requires free public elementary and high school education, compulsory elementary education, and encouragement of non-formal, informal and indigenous learning systems.

**Philippine public schooling** began under the American regime. Act No. 74 (1901) created a Department of Public Instruction, made primary instruction free, and made English the basis of instruction.

## 2. Testable facts

**Sociology of education**
- **Functionalists** view education as one of the most important social institutions. It has **manifest (primary)** functions, which are intended and visible, and **latent (secondary)** functions, which are hidden and unintended. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- The first manifest function is **socialization**. **Émile Durkheim** called schools "socialization agencies" that teach children to get along with others and prepare them for adult economic roles. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Social control** is a manifest function: schools teach conformity to law and respect for authority. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Latent functions** include courtship, social networks that can later help with jobs, and the ability to work with others in small groups. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Conflict theorists** view education as widening social inequality. The **hidden curriculum** is the nonacademic knowledge learned through informal learning and cultural transmission; it favors those with more cultural capital. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Tracking** sorts students into advanced and low tracks. Conflict theorists argue it perpetuates inequality and leads to self-fulfilling prophecies. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Symbolic interactionists** study classroom dynamics and interactions between students and teachers. Labeling, such as calling a student a "low achiever", can become a **self-fulfilling prophecy**. [SRC-0088, 16.2]
- **Feminist theory** studies the roots and effects of gender inequality in education. [SRC-0088, 16.2]

**Inclusive education (RA 11650 and related laws)**
- **Inclusive education** is the process of responding to the diversity of needs of all learners, toward full participation, presence and achievement. It involves **accommodation, modification, adaptation and individualization** in content, approaches, structures and strategies. [SRC-0032, Sec. 4]
- The **policy of inclusion** covers all early and basic education schools, **public and private**. No learner may be **denied admission on the basis of disability**. [SRC-0032, Sec. 5]
- **IEP:** systematic, purposive, developmental programming designed to meet the educational requirements of a learner with disability. It includes the services, their duration and frequency, and the learner's present level. [SRC-0032, Sec. 4]
- DepEd and LGUs shall establish at least one **ILRC** in every city and municipality. **All existing SPED Centers are converted and renamed "Inclusive Learning Resource Center".** [SRC-0032, Sec. 6]
- The ILRC implements the **Child Find System**, identifying, locating and evaluating learners with disabilities who are not receiving education services, and helps include them in the general education system. [SRC-0032, Sec. 7]
- RA 11650's objectives include free and appropriate public early and basic education for learners with disabilities and access to the general education system. [SRC-0032, Sec. 3]
- **Filipino Sign Language** is declared the national sign language of the Filipino deaf (RA 11106). [SRC-0035, title]
- The **Alternative Learning System Act** (RA 11510) institutionalizes ALS for out-of-school children in special cases, youth and adults. [SRC-0037, title]

**Constitutional and historical foundations**
- The State shall protect and promote the right of all citizens to **quality education at all levels** and make it accessible to all. [SRC-0007, Art. XIV Sec. 1]
- The State shall maintain **free public education** in the elementary and high school levels; **elementary education is compulsory** for all children of school age, without limiting parents' natural right to rear their children. [SRC-0007, Art. XIV Sec. 2(2)]
- The State shall encourage **non-formal, informal and indigenous learning systems**. [SRC-0007, Art. XIV Sec. 2(4)]
- **Act No. 74 (1901)** established a Department of Public Instruction. **All primary instruction** in its schools was **free**, and **English** was to be made the basis of all public school instruction "as soon as practicable". [SRC-0011, Secs. 1, 14]

## 3. Common mistakes

- **Manifest vs latent.** Intended and visible (socialization, social control, transmitting culture) = manifest. Unintended by-products (dating, friendships, networking) = latent.
- **Hidden curriculum vs latent function.** Both are "unofficial". The *hidden curriculum* is a **conflict-theory** idea about values and status that reproduce inequality.
- **Labeling or self-fulfilling prophecy** belongs to **symbolic interactionism**. Tracking-as-inequality belongs to **conflict theory**.
- **SPED Center vs ILRC.** Under RA 11650 all SPED Centers became ILRCs. "Inclusion" means learners with disabilities in general education with support, not separate schooling by default.
- **Free vs compulsory.** The Constitution makes public elementary *and* high school *free*, but makes *elementary* education *compulsory*.

## 4. Memory aid

**"Function, Fight, Feel-the-label"**: Functionalism (what schools do for society), conflict (who wins and loses), interactionism (labels in the classroom).
**"SPED → ILRC"**: one per city or municipality, running the Child Find System.

## 5. Sources

- SRC-0088 OpenStax *Introduction to Sociology 3e*, 16.2 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
- SRC-0032 RA 11650 (Secs. 3–7)
- SRC-0035 RA 11106
- SRC-0037 RA 11510
- SRC-0007 1987 Constitution (Art. XIV Secs. 1–2)
- SRC-0011 Act No. 74 (Secs. 1, 14)
- SRC-0001 PRC Res. 11 s. 2025 TOS

title: The professional teacher — licensure, rights and protective laws
md:
# PE-A2 — The professional teacher: licensure, rights and protective laws

The official outline asks you to describe the professional teacher and the high standards of a teacher's personal and professional life, and to explain the roles of a teacher, "with responsibilities as specified in the Code of Ethics for Professional Teachers" [SRC-0001, ProfEd Section A, outcome 2.3]. This lesson covers the laws that make teaching a regulated profession and protect teachers and learners. The Code of Ethics and the PPST get their own lessons once their official texts are in hand (see "Pending" below).

## 1. Plain explanation

**Teaching is a licensed profession.** RA 7836 (1994) is the Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act. It created the **Board for Professional Teachers**, which works under the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC). Nobody may practice as a professional teacher without a certificate of registration and a professional license, unless the law allows an exception such as a special or temporary permit. The LET (officially the LEPT) is the written exam that leads to that license. For secondary teachers it has three parts: general education, professional education and the field of specialization. The law states its aim plainly: the State ensures quality education by regulating the licensure exam and the practice of teaching.

**Who may take the exam** depends on the degree. RA 9293 (2004) changed the rule for graduates outside education: they need at least **18 units** of professional education (the original RA 7836 said 10).

**Public school teachers have a charter of rights**, RA 4670 (1966), the *Magna Carta for Public School Teachers*. It covers:
- workload (6 hours of actual classroom teaching a day)
- job security, consent before transfer, and fair disciplinary procedure
- no discrimination, academic freedom in teaching methods
- fair salaries and no unauthorized salary deductions
- free medical examination, study leave, and the right to organize

**Teachers must keep learning.** RA 10912 (2016) makes continuing professional development (CPD) a requirement for renewing the professional ID.

**Schools must protect learners**, and teachers are part of that system:
- RA 10627 (Anti-Bullying Act) requires every elementary and secondary school to adopt an anti-bullying policy.
- RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act) and RA 11313 (Safe Spaces Act) cover harassment in schools, including by teachers who hold authority over students.
- RA 7610 protects children from abuse.
- RA 9262 covers violence against women and their children, which a teacher may see in a learner's home situation.

## 2. Testable facts

**Licensure (RA 7836 as amended)**
- RA 7836's policy: the State recognizes the vital role of teachers in nation-building and ensures quality education by supervising the licensure exam and professionalizing teaching. [SRC-0016, Sec. 2]
- The Board for Professional Teachers is a collegial body under the general supervision and administrative control of the PRC. It has **5 members** appointed by the President from PRC recommendees chosen from nominees of the accredited teachers' association. [SRC-0016, Sec. 5]
- Board members serve **3-year** terms; a person who has served **two consecutive terms** cannot be reappointed. [SRC-0016, Sec. 7]
- A Board member must be at least **35 years old**, a citizen and resident, of proven integrity, with an education degree. [SRC-0016, Sec. 8]
- Board duties include issuing, suspending or revoking certificates of registration, fixing exam dates and places, and prescribing or adopting a code of ethical and professional standards. [SRC-0016, Sec. 6]
- The written exam must be given **at least once a year**; a valid certificate of registration and professional license are required to practice. [SRC-0016, Sec. 13]
- Secondary-level exam = **three parts**: professional education, general education, field of specialization; elementary = two parts (professional and general education). [SRC-0016, Sec. 14]
- Applicants must be at least **18 years old**, of good health and reputation with high moral values, and not convicted by final judgment of an offense involving moral turpitude. [SRC-0016, Sec. 15]
- The Board reports exam ratings to the PRC within **120 days** after the exam. [SRC-0016, Sec. 16]
- Registration starts when the name is entered in the **roster of professional teachers**; every registrant takes a **professional oath** before practicing. [SRC-0016, Secs. 17–18]
- Teachers may take an optional oral and written **merit examination at least once in 5 years**, free of charge, as a basis for merit promotion. [SRC-0016, Sec. 19]
- After notice and hearing, the Board may suspend or revoke a certificate for causes such as criminal conviction or immoral, unprofessional or dishonorable conduct. [SRC-0016, Sec. 23]
- Practicing without a certificate is punishable by a fine of **P5,000–P20,000** or imprisonment of **6 months to 5 years**, or both. [SRC-0016, Sec. 28]
- RA 9293: graduates of arts and sciences need at least **18 units** of professional education to qualify (originally 10 units under RA 7836). [SRC-0017, Sec. 1; SRC-0016, Sec. 15(e)(3)]
- RA 9293: teachers of vocational and two-year technical courses need a bachelor's degree in their field plus at least **18 units** of professional education. [SRC-0017, Sec. 1]
- RA 9293: registered teachers who have **not practiced for 5 years** must take at least **12 units** of education courses before returning. [SRC-0017, Sec. 2]
- The professional boards prepare the syllabi or TOS, and exam questions must stay strictly within them. [SRC-0018, Sec. 9(h)]

**Magna Carta for Public School Teachers (RA 4670)**
- Minimum qualification for secondary teachers: a bachelor's degree in education with a major and a minor, or an arts or science degree with at least 18 professional units. [SRC-0019, Sec. 3]
- A teacher hired on provisional status for lack of civil service eligibility serves a probation of **at least one year**. [SRC-0019, Sec. 4]
- Security of tenure is assured. A provisional teacher becomes permanent after **at least 10 years** of continuous, efficient, faithful service. [SRC-0019, Sec. 5]
- No transfer **without the teacher's consent**, except for cause. If the service requires a transfer, the superintendent must first notify the teacher of the reasons, and the teacher may appeal. [SRC-0019, Sec. 6]
- Disciplinary safeguards: right to be **informed in writing** of the charges, full access to the evidence, to defend oneself with a representative of choice, and to appeal. No publicity while the case is pending. [SRC-0019, Sec. 8]
- Administrative charges are first heard by a **committee** chaired by the Schools Division Superintendent (or a representative of at least division-supervisor rank), with a teachers' organization representative and a division supervisor. [SRC-0019, Sec. 9]
- No discrimination in entering, practicing or leaving the profession on grounds other than professional ones. [SRC-0019, Sec. 10]
- Married couples who are both public school teachers should, whenever possible, be employed in the same locality. [SRC-0019, Sec. 11]
- Teachers enjoy **academic freedom** in their professional duties, especially in teaching and classroom methods. [SRC-0019, Sec. 12]
- **Teaching hours:** at most **6 hours** of actual classroom teaching a day. Up to **8 hours** when the service requires it, paid at the regular rate **plus at least 25%** of basic pay. [SRC-0019, Sec. 13]
- Co-curricular and out-of-school work beyond normal duties, after 6 hours of teaching, earns at least **25%** additional compensation. [SRC-0019, Sec. 14]
- No salary deductions except as authorized by law. With the teacher's written authority, teachers' association dues and insurance premiums may be deducted. [SRC-0019, Sec. 21]
- Compulsory **free medical examination** before starting to teach, repeated **at least once a year**. [SRC-0019, Sec. 22]
- Physical and nervous strain on the teacher's health is recognized as a compensable occupational disease. [SRC-0019, Sec. 23]
- **Study leave:** up to **one school year** after **7 years** of service, at **at least 60%** of monthly salary. [SRC-0019, Sec. 24]
- **Indefinite sick leave** when an illness needs treatment exceeding one year. [SRC-0019, Sec. 25]
- On retirement, a **one-range salary raise** is the basis for computing retirement benefits. [SRC-0019, Sec. 26]
- Teachers may freely **establish and join organizations** without prior authorization. Making employment conditional on not joining is prohibited discrimination. [SRC-0019, Secs. 27–28]

**Continuing professional development (RA 10912)**
- CPD is a **mandatory requirement** for renewing the professional identification card of every PRC-regulated professional. [SRC-0030, Sec. 10]
- CPD programs aim to upgrade competencies in line with the Philippine Qualifications Framework (PQF), the ASEAN Qualifications Reference Framework (AQRF) and ASEAN mutual recognition arrangements. [SRC-0030, Sec. 4]

**Protecting learners**
- **Bullying** (RA 10627) is any severe or repeated use by one or more students of written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, directed at another student, causing fear of harm, a hostile environment, infringement of rights, or disruption of the educational process. [SRC-0025, Sec. 2]
- **All elementary and secondary schools** must adopt anti-bullying policies, including bans on bullying on and near school grounds, at school activities, through school technology, and **retaliation** against those who report. [SRC-0025, Sec. 3]
- The **school principal** (or equivalent) is responsible for implementing anti-bullying policies. School staff, students, parents and volunteers must report bullying they witness. [SRC-0025, Sec. 4]
- Schools report their anti-bullying policies in writing to the **schools division superintendent** within 6 months of the law taking effect, then report bullying statistics every first week of the school year. [SRC-0025, Sec. 5]
- **Education-related sexual harassment** (RA 7877) is committed by a teacher, instructor, professor, coach or trainer who, having **authority, influence or moral ascendancy**, demands, requests or requires a sexual favor, **whether or not the demand is accepted**. [SRC-0026, Sec. 3]
- The **Safe Spaces Act** (RA 11313) requires every school, public or private, to designate an officer to receive complaints and to adopt and publish grievance procedures. [SRC-0027, Sec. 21]
- School heads must post the Safe Spaces Act, run prevention measures, and create an independent mechanism to investigate complaints. [SRC-0027, Sec. 22]
- **Children** (RA 7610) means persons **below 18**, or older persons unable to protect themselves because of a physical or mental disability or condition. [SRC-0029, Sec. 3(a)]
- **Child abuse** includes psychological and physical abuse, neglect, cruelty, sexual abuse and emotional maltreatment, and acts that debase or demean a child's dignity. [SRC-0029, Sec. 3(b)]
- **VAWC** (RA 9262) covers physical, sexual and psychological harm and economic abuse by a husband, former husband, or a man the woman had a sexual or dating relationship or a common child with, against the woman or her child. [SRC-0028, Sec. 3(a)]

**The Constitution on teachers**
- The State shall enhance the right of teachers to professional advancement. [SRC-0007, Art. XIV Sec. 5(4)]
- The State shall give the **highest budgetary priority** to education and ensure that teaching attracts and retains its rightful share of the best talents. [SRC-0007, Art. XIV Sec. 5(5)]

## 3. Common mistakes

- **RA 7836 vs RA 9293 vs RA 4670.** RA 7836 = licensure and the Board. RA 9293 = amended licensure eligibility (18 units; 12-unit refresher). RA 4670 = rights of *public* school teachers. A question about "who may take the LET" is never RA 4670.
- **"RA 4670 gives free legal assistance."** The text of RA 4670 contains no such provision. Do not choose it on that basis.
- **6 vs 8 hours.** The cap is 6 hours of *actual classroom teaching*. 8 hours is the absolute maximum, allowed only when the service requires it and only with extra pay of at least 25%.
- **Study leave numbers.** It comes after 7 years of service, lasts at most one school year, and pays at least 60% of salary. Swapping 7 and 10 (the years to permanent status) is a classic trap.
- **Board size and terms.** 5 members, 3-year terms, no more than two consecutive terms. Board members must be at least 35; examinees at least 18.
- **Bullying is student-to-student** under RA 10627's definition. A teacher harassing a student falls under RA 7877 or RA 11313, or child abuse under RA 7610, not the Anti-Bullying Act.
- **Sexual harassment needs no acceptance and no physical contact.** RA 7877 is committed by the demand or request itself, whether or not it is accepted.
- **CPD** is tied to renewing the professional ID card, not to taking the LET.

## 4. Memory aid

**"5-3-35, 6-8-25, 7-1-60"**
- **Board:** 5 members, 3-year terms, members at least 35.
- **Teaching day:** 6 hours normal, 8 at most, +25% pay for the extra.
- **Study leave:** after 7 years, for 1 school year, at 60% pay.
